text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: We should implement high-contrast focus rings that appear immediately upon keyboard navigation. This visually aids users relying on keyboard navigation, ensuring they can easily see which element is active and improving overall usability. The trade-off here is the potential for visual distractions for mouse users, but the increased accessibility for keyboard users outweighs this concern. Making sure all users can effectively navigate the interface is our priority.

name: Reader
text: High-contrast focus rings risk creating a visual "siren" effect, overwhelming users with low vision or cognitive disabilities. A better alternative is a subtle focus ring that still meets WCAG contrast but avoids drawing excessive attention. Settle this by testing both options with users who rely on keyboard navigation and measure task completion time and reported comfort.

name: Ramp
text:
We should implement a subtle focus ring that meets WCAG contrast standards, as it provides a clear indicator of focus for keyboard users while avoiding the "siren" effect that could overwhelm users with low vision or cognitive disabilities. This approach strikes a balance between usability and visual accessibility, making EXCAVA more inclusive for a broader range of users. The trade-off is that the subtle focus ring may not be as immediately noticeable as a high-contrast one, potentially requiring more user interaction to become apparent. By opting for a subtle focus ring, we prioritize reducing visual distractions over maximizing focus visibility.

name: Reader
text: A subtle focus ring may still not provide sufficient visibility for all users, especially those with low vision. The risk remains that it could lead to confusion or difficulty in determining which element is active. To settle this, conduct user testing with a diverse group, including those with varying levels of visual ability, to evaluate the effectiveness of both subtle and high-contrast focus rings in real-world scenarios.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Ship a **user-customizable focus indicator** that includes both a **subtle high-contrast focus ring** and an **immediate high-contrast option**, tested for usability by a diverse group, owned by the accessibility team.
